newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish PM to consult on farm minister's dismissal.
newsitem.headline: Polish PM to consult on farm minister's dismissal.

text.p: Polish Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz said he would meet leaders of the co-ruling Peasant Party (PSL) on Tuesday to discuss their demand to fire the agriculture minister.
"On Tuesday I will meet Peasant officials and the meeting will be connected with their motion to dismiss minister (Roman) Jagielinski," Cimoszewicz told a news conference on Monday.
Last week, the executive of the PSL, the ruling coalition's smaller party, withdrew support for Jagielinski, who is considered among the more liberal of Peasant party politicians.
The body alleged that the minister had implemented wrong agricultural policies, which led to a $1 billion food trade deficit last year.

Cimoszewicz, a leader of the coalition's larger ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance, had earlier been quoted as saying he would decide on Jagielinski's dismissal after the meeting with the Peasant leadership.
He said on Monday he disagreed with the criticism of the government's farm policies which had been pursued by the minister.

Jagielinski, who has been exposed in his own party since he unsuccessfully challenged Pawlak for its leadership last year, said he would not resign on his own and left the decision up to the prime minister.
He has questioned the right of the Peasant's executive committee, rather than the full party council, to dismiss him.
